title: Implement retry with exponential backoff
instruction:
Write a loop that retries a request up to 3 times when the status code is 429 (rate limited). Use an exponential backoff delay: 1 second for the first retry, 2 for the second, 4 for the third. Print "Waiting {n} seconds..." before each retry.

Simulate with a function `fake_request()` that returns a mock response with status code 429 for the first 2 calls, then 200 on the 3rd.
starter_code:
attempt = 0
max_retries = 3

# Simulate a rate-limited API
responses = [429, 429, 200]

def fake_request():
    global attempt
    result = responses[attempt]
    attempt += 1
    # Return an object with .status_code
    class MockResponse:
        pass
    r = MockResponse()
    r.status_code = result
    return r

# Call fake_request(), check status, retry with backoff if 429
solution_code:
attempt = 0
max_retries = 3
responses = [429, 429, 200]

def fake_request():
    global attempt
    result = responses[attempt]
    attempt += 1
    class MockResponse:
        pass
    r = MockResponse()
    r.status_code = result
    return r

for i in range(max_retries):
    response = fake_request()
    if response.status_code == 200:
        print("Success!")
        break
    elif response.status_code == 429:
        wait = 2 ** i
        print(f"Waiting {wait} seconds...")
    else:
        print(f"Error: {response.status_code}")
        break

title: Use raise_for_status() correctly
instruction:
Write code that makes a GET request to `https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1`, uses `raise_for_status()` to check for errors, and if successful, parses the JSON and prints the `title` field.

Wrap the call in a try/except that catches `requests.exceptions.HTTPError` and prints "HTTP error occurred".
starter_code:
import requests

try:
    response = requests.get("https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1")
    # Use raise_for_status() here
    # Parse and print the title
except requests.exceptions.HTTPError:
    print("HTTP error occurred")
solution_code:
import requests

try:
    response = requests.get("https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1")
    response.raise_for_status()
    data = response.json()
    print(data["title"])
except requests.exceptions.HTTPError:
    print("HTTP error occurred")

test_cases.expected_output: sunt aut facere repellat provident occaecati excepturi optio reprehenderit

title: Understand automatic redirect following
instruction:

Make a GET request to `http://httpbin.org/redirect/1` (which returns a 302 redirect) with `allow_redirects=False`. Print the status code and the `Location` header.

response = requests.get("http://httpbin.org/redirect/1", allow_redirects=False)
